findings.title: Pairing can durably commit a device before credential custody is established
Mobile WebSocket commands bypass granted chat/media scopes
Refresh rotation can strand a paired device on ambiguous delivery
Versioned mobile route contract contradicts the production edge
Isolated mobile data server exercises materially different authorization and recovery semantics
Systemd supervision reports applied success without checking command success
Pairing can proceed without a verified Tailscale Serve mapping
Manual 8-digit pairing cannot survive Android process/activity recreation after collection
Mobile HTTP completions can arrive before request correlation is armed
A valid large WebSocket frame can permanently wedge the JNI event pump
Android logcat receives replayable signed-media bearer capabilities
Global native last_error storage is unsafe under concurrent Android calls
Bounded broker event pressure can silently drop admitted operation completions
The 512 MiB native media-cache budget is enforced only after unbounded single-file writes
Phone-side Pairing Cancel is not durable and can resume into approval after restart
Release signing material is exposed to dependency-rich pre-sign build steps
The pinned mobile toolchain accepts stale/unverified cached tools and an ambient Bun
Gradle wrapper distribution is not cryptographically pinned
Desktop-parity checker silently skips async inbound-command and misc-route source coverage
Update-persistence qualification reinstalls the same APK instead of exercising an actual upgrade

final_discussion_questions.question: D2/D4: Is owner intended to imply every chat/media/attachment capability, or should reduced owner scopes remain an enforceable ceiling across HTTP and typed WebSocket commands?
D5/D6: What common credential-handoff receipt should pairing and refresh use so issued/applied-but-not-received becomes retry-safe?
D4/D6: What is the authoritative pairing lifecycle across QR/manual collection, Cancel, process restart, expiry, Tailscale readiness and desktop approval?
D5/D6/D7: Should native HTTP/WS requests use one completion owner with atomic correlation, guaranteed terminal delivery and applied/not-applied/uncertain outcomes?
D6/D7: What single frame/event-size budget should apply end-to-end across WebUI, Capacitor/Kotlin, JNI and the Go broker?
D2/D7: What is the lifetime/secrecy model for signed media capabilities, and what hard persistent-storage budget should media streaming/cache enforce?
D4/P01: Which artifact is the source of truth for mobile routes/operations/parity, and should production dispatch, generated contracts and parity tests derive from it?
D2/Q01: What release-build trust boundary should receive signing credentials, and must every compiler/package manager/SDK/Gradle distribution be verified before signing?
D4/D6/Q01: What baseline/candidate artifact policy should qualify real Android upgrades, custody schema evolution and embedded Tailscale-state migration?
D4/D6: Should local systemd/Tailscale setup remain opt-in best-effort tooling or become product-owned lifecycle/readiness with exact success and Serve semantics?

cross_module_dependencies_and_conflicts: E02 owns shared WebUI route/settings/server contracts; R01 owns the paired-device/mobile authorization and transport consequence, especially F02/F04/F19.
D01/U01 own broader client/recovery lifecycle; R01 owns Android/native correlation, pairing and transport-state failures.
T01/A01 should share the final applied/not-applied/uncertain effect receipt model with remote credential/completion paths.
K01/Q01 overlap release subprocess/toolchain trust; R01 owns the concrete Android signing path in F16-F18.
P01 should reconcile route/operation contract generation and retirement of legacy or substitute mobile transport declarations.
M01/X01/Q01 remain queued and may own broader mobile ingress/package/performance concerns; R01 publication does not pre-empt those denominators.
